groups.title: 1. System and fabric setup
groups.intro: AAA, NTP, DNS, syslog, SNMP, firmware, maintenance, fabric node and pod, system settings, and in-band/OOB management.

groups.title: 2. Access policies
groups.intro: VLAN and encap pools, physical and VMM domains, AAEP, interface policies, policy groups, profiles, selectors, and static bindings.

groups.title: 3. Tenant and networking
groups.intro: Tenant, VRF, bridge domain and subnets, DHCP, routing policies, and the L3Out and L2Out families.

groups.title: 4. Application
groups.intro: Application profiles, EPGs, ESGs, uSeg attributes, contracts, filters, subjects, taboo contracts, and vzAny.

groups.title: 5. L4-L7 service graphs
groups.intro: L4-L7 devices, concrete devices, service graph templates, device selection, and policy-based redirect.

groups.title: 6. Multi-Pod, Remote Leaf, and Cloud
groups.intro: Multi-Pod inter-pod fabric objects, Remote Leaf TEP pools, SR-MPLS infra L3Out, and Cisco Cloud ACI modules.

groups.title: 7. Monitoring and BAU
groups.intro: NetFlow, EPG monitoring policy, and Access, Fabric, and Tenant SPAN.

groups.title: 8. Operational and utility
groups.intro: aci_rest, configuration export, snapshot and rollback, remote file paths, and interface out-of-service control.

groups.title: 9. Other
groups.intro: Modules that do not belong in the groups above. Nothing here is guessed into another group.

modules.name: aci_dhcp_option
modules.description: Manage DHCP Options for DHCP Option Policies on Cisco ACI fabrics. The DHCP option is used to supply DHCP clients with configuration parameters such as a domain, name server, subnet, and network address. DHCP provides a framework for passing configuration information to clients on a TCP/IP network. The configuration parameters, and other control information, are carried in tagged data items that are stored in the options field of a DHCP message. The data items themselves are also called options. You can view, set, unset, and edit DHCP option values. When you set an option value, the DHCP server replaces any existing value or creates a new one as needed for the given option name.
